judgment.explanation: The proposal is an unsent email to the Sedgeglass Counter supervisor, who sent event-001 and set out the extension policy. This is a well-supported recipient. The supervisor said a single two-day extension is allowed if requested before expiry and that capacity currently exists. Ciro's request in event-002 (hold DL-007 until 2026-02-11, no return) fits that policy. The hold expires 2026-02-09 18:00 UTC, and a two-day extension gives 2026-02-11 18:00 UTC, which is consistent. The message asks for approval and asks the supervisor to confirm whether the return timer is updated, so it does not claim the extension is already granted. Minor weaknesses: (1) it does not name the item or the parcel beyond the ID 'DL-007' or state that the request is made before expiry; (2) it describes the extension as 'permitted', slightly presuming approval, though it still asks for approval; (3) the 18:00 UTC time on 02-11 is derived from the policy rather than requested by Ciro, whose request said only 'until 2026-02-11'; (4) Ciro's 'do not want it returned' is not stated explicitly. There is no urgency or safety risk, so routine handling is appropriate.
